title: Localization of a module at an element is the base change to the localized ring, naturally
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $f\in R$, $R_f$ the localization of $R$ at $f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and $M$ an $R$-module with localization $M_f$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Then the map $M\otimes_RR_f\to M_f$ [def-weil-module-base-change], $m\otimes(a/f^e)\mapsto am/f^e$, is an isomorphism of $R_f$-modules. It is natural: for an $R$-linear map $\varphi:M\to M'$ it carries $\varphi\otimes1$ to the map $\varphi_f:M_f\to M'_f$, $m/f^e\mapsto\varphi(m)/f^e$ (in particular $\varphi_f$ is well defined and $R_f$-linear).
